records.subject: STAT
records.title: Introduction to Statistical Methods
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103, 105, or 251, each with a C or better, or credit for MATH 106, 108, 140, 171, 201, 202, 252, or DATA 212, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 45%, or transfer credit for Intermediate Algebra equivalent to MATH 101.
records.description: Introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics: t-tests, chi-square tests, one-way ANOVA, simple linear regression and correlation.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Probability and Statistics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 140, 171, 202, or DATA 121 each with a C or better, or MATH 172 or 182.
records.description: Probability models, sample spaces, random variables, distributions, moments, comparative experiments, tests, correlation and regression in engineering applications. Credit not granted for both STAT 360 and 370.  (Crosslisted course offered as STAT 360, DATA 360.)

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Introductory Statistics for Engineers
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 140, 171, 202 or DATA 121 each with a C or better, or MATH 172 or 182.
records.description: Probability axioms, probability models, random variables, expectation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, control charts. Credit not granted for both STAT 360 and 370.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Decision Making and Statistics
records.description: Concepts and methods of decision science using simple mathematical, statistical and computer based tools to solve complex problems for sound decision making.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Topics in Probability and Statistics
records.description: Current topics in probability and statistics of mutual interest to faculty and students. Recommended preparation:  One 3-hour 300-level STAT course. Credit not granted for both STAT 410 and STAT 510.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Statistical Methods in Research I
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: STAT 212, MATH 140, 171, 202, or DATA 121, or graduate standing.
records.description: Intermediate statistical methods, design and analysis of research studies: completely randomized and randomized block designs, multiple regression, categorical data analysis.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Introduction to Multivariate Statistics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 220, 225, or 230; one 300-400-level STAT.
records.description: Introductory course covering multidimensional data, multivariate normal distribution, principal components, factor analysis, clustering, and discriminant analysis.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Sampling Methods
records.description: Simple and stratified random sampling; systematic sampling; cluster sampling; double sampling, area sampling.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Statistical Methods for Engineers and Scientists
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 140, 171, 202,  or DATA 121, each with a C or better, or MATH 172 or 182.
records.description: Hypothesis testing; linear, multilinear, and nonlinear regression; analysis of variance for designed experiments; quality control; statistical computing. Recommended preparation:  One 3-credit 300-level STAT course. Credit not granted for both STAT 423 and STAT 523. Credit not normally granted for both STAT 423 and 430.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Statistical Modeling for Data Analytics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: STAT/DATA 360 or STAT 370, either with a C or better.
records.description: Multiple linear regression with model selection, dealing with multicollinearity, assessing model assumptions, the LASSO, ridge regression, elastic nets, Loess smoothing, logistic regression, Poisson regression, and the application of the bootstrap to regression modeling.  (Crosslisted course offered as STAT 435, DATA 435.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: High Dimensional Data Learning and Visualization
records.description: Data visualization, metric-based clustering, probabilistic and metric-based classification, algebraic and probabilistic dimension reduction, scalable inferential methods, analysis of non-Euclidean data.  (Crosslisted course offered as STAT 437, DATA 437.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Applied Probability
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 172 or MATH 182; MATH 220, MATH 225, or MATH 230.
records.description: Axioms of probability theory; random variables; expectation; generating function; law of large numbers; central limit theorem; Markov chains.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Statistical Applications in Insurance
records.description: Introduction to the application of mathematics and statistics to the insurance field with a focus on actuarial science.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Introduction to Time Series Analysis
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: STAT 412 or concurrent enrollment, or STAT 423 or concurrent enrollment.
records.description: Introduction to the analysis and application of time series including AR, MA, ARMA, and ARIMA models.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Introduction to Statistical Theory
records.description: Sampling distributions; hypothesis testing and estimation; maximum likelihood; likelihood ratio tests; theory of least squares; nonparametrics. Recommended preparation: One 3-credit 400-level STAT or probability course. (Crosslisted course offered as STAT 456, MATH 456.) Credit not granted for more than one of STAT/MATH 456 or STAT 556.

records.subject: STAT
records.title: Statistical Foundations in Artificial Intelligence
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: DATA 219; DATA 324; MATH 216; STAT/DATA 360.
records.description: Statistical foundations of AI, including data ethics, probability for generative models, inference, predictive modeling, statistical learning, and deep learning, emphasizing theory, real-world applications, and ethical implications.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
